annotations.annotation_text: HCE manifestation "porter" on page 136 within "The Quiz Chapter": here the universal father-figure Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker appears in the context of twelve questions and answers probing HCE's identity, the Mookse and the Gripes parable, Professor Jones. annotations.annotation_text: Tavern/jury motif "porter" on page 136 ("The Quiz Chapter"): the twelve customers drinking in HCE's Chapelizod pub represent public opinion, the Zodiac, and the Apostles within twelve questions and answers probing HCE's identity, the Mookse and the Gripes parable, Professor Jones. During this Age of Gods phase, they judge, condemn, and demand another round — the Greek chorus of middle-class Dublin gossip.

annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "darkness" on page 136 ("The Quiz Chapter"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within twelve questions and answers probing HCE's identity, the Mookse and the Gripes parable, Professor Jones. During this Age of Gods phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.
